context: a letter from John (b) Murray, which you are answering
exchanges:
I have made up the account of the new Edition of Darwin on Species—of wch I have now disposed of about 700 copies—& have much pleasure in enclosing a Cheque for £250" being ⅔ ds. of the estimated profits—allowing £50" for advertising of wch £30’ have been actually expended—

I enclose also the account of The Orchids, by wch you will perceive that the deficiency has been considerably reduced—

I remain My Dear Sir | Yours very faithfully | John Murray

I hope I have found a suitable Index-maker. I will ask for a sample for your approval

Chas Darwin Esq

I acknowledge receipt & thank you for the very pleasant remittance of £250 for the 4th. Edit. of Origin.—

I enclose cheque for Presentation Copies; be so kind as to return me the enclosed receipted.— I am very glad to see that Orchid Book does sell a little. I hope the new Book will be more successful; but Heaven only knows.

I think it will be a very good plan that I may see a portion of Index, before, I presume, it is arranged alphabetically & I will compare it with the early sheets.—

With my ⁠⟨⁠best than⁠⟩⁠ks | yours very sincerely | Ch. Darwin
